messages:
From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@greenstack.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@greenstack.com>, GreenStack Procurement <procurement@greenstack.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal pricing & capacity escalation

Hi Priya,

Quick background — GreenStack saw a 3x spike in inference volume in Q2 after a partner launch. Our usage forecasts for the next 12 months are materially higher than the current commit. We're approaching our renewal window (current term ends 10/15) and procurement is asking for two things before we move forward:

1) A temporary price hold for the first 3 months of the next term while we stabilize our traffic patterns (we need a fixed per-token rate during ramp).
2) Some form of bridging credit or one-time offset to account for the Q2 spike that pushed us over committed thresholds.

We are open to increasing committed capacity (we'd consider a staged commit) but need to avoid significant overage unpredictability in the first quarter of the renewal. Can you send a proposed structure (pricing, credits, and rollout cadence) that we can review with finance this week?

Attached: usage_report_q2.pdf (summary + traffic heatmap).

Thanks,
Maria
Maria Garcia
Head of Platform Operations | GreenStack Technologies

Cc: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@greenstack.com>, GreenStack Procurement <procurement@greenstack.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing & capacity escalation

Hi Maria —

Thanks for the context and the report; that spike makes sense given the partner rollout. We can absolutely flex on a renewal structure that reduces short-term variability while allowing you to scale. High-level proposal below; I'm happy to put numbers to it and send a one-page termsheet for legal/ procurement:

- Term: 12 months with an optional 6-month extension (mutually agreed).
- Price hold: We can lock your current per-token rate for the first 90 days of the new term. After that, rates revert to the negotiated tiered schedule tied to monthly consumption bands.
- Bridging credit: Provide a one-time credit equal to 15% of Q2 overage spend, applied to the first invoice of the new term.
- Commit: Staged commit increase — 50% of anticipated uplift effective day 1, automatic lift to full commit at month 4 contingent on observed traffic (we can define the metric/signal).
- Overage guard: Cap maximum overage rate at 20% above committed price for months 1–3 to reduce surprise.

If that aligns, I will loop in Finance/Legal for draft redlines and provide a mutual action plan. CC'ing Ben (sales lead) and Karthik (solutions) to confirm operational feasibility. I will also attach a draft MAP and a redline template in my next note.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (stub)

Subject: Fwd: Renewal pricing & capacity escalation — internal proposal

Team — forwarding GreenStack thread. Key asks: 3-month price hold, bridging credit, staged commit. Suggested commercial parameters (numbers are placeholders — need finance sign-off):

- 12m term; 90-day price hold at current effective rate ($0.0009/token).
- Bridging credit = 15% of measured Q2 overage (~$48,000 per customer's calc).
- Commit: day-1 commit increase of 50% of forecasted uplift (to reduce immediate spikes), ramp to 100% at month 4 if traffic >= 75% of forecasted uplift for 30 days.
- Overage cap = committed rate + 20% for months 1–3.

Questions for Finance/Legal (Laura):
1) Is 15% credit on overage acceptable vs. an absolute $ credit?
2) Any restrictions around a time-limited price hold we should flag in the contract?
3) For staged commit automation, do we need a manual signoff or can we automate based on telemetry?

Ben/Karthik — operationally, can we guarantee burst capacity in months 1–3 without SLA risk? If not, we should add a fallback model that routes excess to an alternative model variant.

Please reply with edits; I aim to surface a clean termsheet to GreenStack by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Priya
